mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically for four consecutive weeks (-35.3 to -29.9), indicating sustained recovery momentum in shopping and recreation activity that should continue extrapolating upward over the next month absent a shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved each of the last 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days falls below the last 28-day mean despite the prior 4-week monotonic improvement trend.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility jumped from -8.4 to +7.7 in a single week, crossing above baseline, which signals a seasonal shift toward outdoor recreation that substitutes for indoor retail and recreation visits, pulling RETAIL_REC growth down over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses above 0 percent change from baseline week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -8.4 to +7.7 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next two weeks even as PARKS remains elevated above baseline.

evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improved every week in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 4 weeks even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both continue improving jointly.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has been gradually declining (10.9 to 8.1), suggesting a relaxation of stay-at-home policy pressure or guidance; under an easing-restrictions regime this reduced home-confinement should translate into higher retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined every week from 10.9 to 8.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 4 weeks despite continued decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The pace of improvement in TRANSIT has slowed sharply between t-2w and t-1w (32.4 to 31.7, less than 1 point change) compared to earlier weeks, suggesting behavioral habituation to current mobility levels; once TRANSIT plateaus, RETAIL_REC gains should also decelerate rather than reverse over the next two weeks.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth rate accelerates rather than decelerates over the next 2 weeks despite TRANSIT plateauing.

candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose 16.1 points in the most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week immediately following a greater-than-10-point PARKS jump.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility remains deeply negative (-21.1) despite incremental improvement, indicating continued remote-work policy enforcement; as long as workplace attendance stays suppressed, weekday-driven retail traffic will remain structurally capped, limiting RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES remains below -20 throughout the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises substantially over the next 4 weeks even though WORKPLACES remains below -20.

evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -5.3 to -0.7 while TRANSIT improved from -36.6 to -30.4
